answer: Cross-subsidy coordination pricing. Each agent posts a recurring coordination fee proportional to the number of distinct peers it transacts with in an epoch; the fee funds a shared signal pool that subsidizes low-degree agents. A sybil cluster must pay the full peer-count fee for every synthetic edge it creates, so faking N identities costs N times the marginal coordination price, while a genuine oasis of sparse agents pays near zero. The trellis of real transactions stays cheap; manufactured density is taxed at its true coordination load.
